records.name: Church random sequence (Church's 1940 effective selection formulation)
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence with limiting digit frequency p
records.effective_resources: effectively calculable selection rule whose choice at each stage depends on previously seen terms, in Church's formulation
records.measure_assumptions: frequency formulation rather than an explicit measure-test definition
records.formal_summary: A sequence is admitted as random only if its limiting frequency is p and every infinite subsequence selected by an effectively calculable admissible rule retains limiting frequency p.
cautions: Later literature uses related terms such as Church stochasticity; P1-S001 does not assert identity across all conventions without a dedicated terminology check.

records.name: Martin-Löf randomness on fair-coin Cantor space
records.effective_resources: uniformly computably enumerable sequence of effectively open sets
records.measure_assumptions: uniform/fair-coin measure; test levels have measure at most 2^-n
records.relativization: oracle variants exist but are not defined in P1-S001
records.formal_summary: A Martin-Löf test is a uniformly c.e. sequence of effectively open sets with μ(U_n) ≤ 2^-n. X is Martin-Löf random iff it is not in the intersection of any Martin-Löf test (equivalently, it passes every such test).

records.name: Schnorr randomness
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / real in fair-coin Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: uniformly c.e. open test levels with an effectively controlled measure: in SRC-0008, μ(U_n)≤2^-n and n↦μ(U_n) is computable; SRC-0024/SRC-0028 use the equivalent exact-measure normalization μ(U_n)=2^-n
records.framework: effective null tests with computable level measures; equivalent bounded-rate computable-martingale and total-Solovay formulations are separately indexed
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space in the inspected primary formulations
records.relativization: not normalized for Schnorr randomness in P1-S002; no oracle convention is promoted here without a dedicated relativization pass
records.formal_summary: A sequence is Schnorr random iff it passes every uniformly effective open test whose level measures are themselves computable. The 2002 primary formulation uses μ(U_n)≤2^-n with computable n↦μ(U_n); later primary sources inspected here use an exact μ(U_n)=2^-n normal form.

source_support.pointer: preprint p. 4; retained P1-S001 survey provenance

cautions: P1-S001 provenance is preserved. P1-S002 corrects a convention ambiguity: computable level measures are the substantive Schnorr restriction; μ(U_n)=2^-n is an inspected normal-form convention, not the only baseline statement.
The original 1971 Schnorr book/article are catalogued as SRC-0022/SRC-0023 at METADATA_ONLY; their internal statements were not silently substituted.

records.name: Computable randomness
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / subset A of N identified with its characteristic sequence
records.effective_resources: total computable (historically: recursive) martingales; rational-valued martingales suffice in the inspected primary formulations
records.framework: betting / martingale; equivalent computably graded effective tests are indexed separately
records.relativization: not normalized in P1-S002; later oracle variants require a dedicated source pass
records.formal_summary: A sequence X is computably random iff no computable martingale has unbounded capital along X, i.e. no computable martingale M has limsup_n M(X↾n)=∞.

source_support.pointer: preprint p. 4; retained P1-S001 survey provenance

cautions: 'Recursive randomness' is recorded as a historical/source term for this computable-martingale notion, not as a blanket alias for every historical use of 'recursive random'.

records.name: Martin-Löf test for a computable measure on Cantor space
records.object_domain: Cantor space 2^ω equipped with computable probability measure μ
records.formal_summary: A test is a uniformly effectively open sequence (U_n) with μ(U_n) ≤ 2^-n; the intersection is an effective μ-null set, and a point is μ-random when it avoids every such effective null set.

records.name: Uniform randomness test over computable probability measures
records.object_domain: pair (μ,x), with μ a computable probability measure and x a point in the represented/computable metric-space framework
records.effective_resources: positive lower-semicomputable test function uniform in the measure parameter
records.measure_assumptions: test t satisfies an integral bound (≤1) with respect to μ in the inspected formulation
records.relativization: uniformity is in the measure parameter; oracle relativization not treated here
records.formal_summary: Hoyrup and Rojas formulate tests uniformly in the probability measure using lower-semicomputable nonnegative functions with bounded μ-integral, and define a point as random when it has finite value for every such test.

records.name: Kolmogorov–Loveland randomness
records.effective_resources: computable non-monotonic betting strategies that may choose which bit to bet on next
records.measure_assumptions: binary fair-betting setting of inspected source abstract
records.formal_summary: X is KL-random iff no computable non-monotonic betting strategy succeeds on X with unbounded gain while successively betting on bits of X.
cautions: The coincidence question with Martin-Löf randomness is QST-0001, not an established equivalence.

records.name: Low for Martin-Löf randomness
records.effective_resources: comparison of unrelativized and A-relative Martin-Löf randomness
records.measure_assumptions: standard fair-coin setting in source abstract
records.relativization: intrinsic: A is used as oracle
records.formal_summary: A is low for Martin-Löf randomness if every unrelativized Martin-Löf random set remains Martin-Löf random relative to A.

records.name: K-triviality
records.relativization: not part of the definition recorded here
records.formal_summary: A is K-trivial if K(A↾n) ≤ K(n)+O(1) for all n.

records.name: Base for R-randomness
records.object_domain: set B relative to a specified randomness notion R
records.relativization: essential: Z is R-random relative to B
records.formal_summary: B is a base for R-randomness if there exists Z ≥_T B such that Z is R-random relative to B.

records.name: Plain Kolmogorov complexity C
records.effective_resources: fixed optimal description machine in the plain-machine model
records.formal_summary: C(σ) is the length of a shortest description/program for σ on a fixed optimal plain description machine, up to the usual additive-machine constant.

records.name: Prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity K
records.formal_summary: K(σ) is the length of a shortest prefix-free description/program for σ on a fixed optimal prefix-free machine, up to an additive constant.

records.name: Kurtz randomness
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / real α in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: computably enumerable (Σ^0_1) measure-one open classes in the weak-1 formulation
records.framework: measure-one effective typicality test; equivalent weak-test/martingale formulations are source-supported in SRC-0029
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space; tested class has measure 1
records.relativization: SRC-0027 supports the weak-n family and states relative randomness is obtained by adding an oracle to tests; no standalone oracle-Kurtz record is created here
records.formal_summary: α is Kurtz random iff α belongs to every computably enumerable (Σ^0_1) class of measure one; equivalently it avoids every effectively closed null class.

source_support.pointer: publisher abstract explicitly states the definition

cautions: Unqualified 'Kurtz randomness' / 'weak randomness' denotes the n=1 level here. Weak 2-randomness is strictly stronger and is not treated as an alias.
SRC-0025 is the original Kurtz thesis but remains METADATA_ONLY; exact definition support comes from inspected later primary sources.

records.name: Weak n-randomness
records.object_domain: real α in Cantor space 2^ω, with integer n≥1
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure; α must belong to every Σ^0_n class of measure 1
records.relativization: SRC-0027 explicitly says relative randomness is obtained in the usual way by adding an oracle to tests; its comparison notion n-randomness is the relativized Martin-Löf level
records.formal_summary: For n≥1, α is weakly n-random iff it belongs to every Σ^0_n class of measure one.
cautions: The adjective 'weak' is indexed by n; it must not be collapsed into unqualified Kurtz/weak randomness without the level.

records.name: Weak 2-randomness
records.effective_resources: avoidance of Π^0_2 nullsets; equivalently computable nested c.e.-open tests whose measures converge to 0 without an effective rate
records.framework: Π^0_2 nullset avoidance / generalized Martin-Löf tests
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure; generalized-test level measures tend to zero
records.relativization: SRC-0027 states relative randomness is obtained by adding an oracle to the tests
records.formal_summary: α is weakly 2-random iff it avoids every Π^0_2 nullset; equivalently it passes every generalized Martin-Löf test. The key contrast with Martin-Löf tests is that μ(U_n)→0 need not have a computable convergence rate.
cautions: Weak 2-randomness is a higher Kurtz/weak-n level and is not synonymous with unqualified Kurtz randomness (weak 1-randomness).

records.name: Generalized Martin-Löf test (for weak 2-randomness)
records.object_domain: computable sequence (U_n) of c.e. open subsets of Cantor space
records.effective_resources: uniform c.e. openness and computable indexing; no required computable modulus for measure convergence
records.relativization: SRC-0027 states oracle-relative versions are obtained by adding an oracle to the tests
records.formal_summary: A generalized Martin-Löf test is a computable nested sequence of c.e. open sets U_n with μ(U_n)→0. Unlike an ML test it imposes no prescribed/effective speed of convergence.

source_support.pointer: Definition 2.2 and following sentence on speed of convergence

records.name: Total Solovay test (Schnorr form)
records.object_domain: computable sequence (V_i) of c.e. open subsets of Cantor space
records.effective_resources: uniformly effective enumeration plus computability of the finite total measure sum
records.measure_assumptions: Σ_i μ(V_i) is finite and is a computable real
records.relativization: not treated in the inspected source record
records.formal_summary: A total Solovay test is a computable collection of c.e. open sets whose sum of measures is finite and computable; a real passes if it belongs to only finitely many levels.

records.name: Computably graded test
records.object_domain: Martin-Löf test (V_n) on Cantor space equipped with a computable grading map f:2^{<ω}×ω→R
records.effective_resources: computable grading f controlling conditional/local level measure over cylinders and finite prefix-free refinements
records.framework: restricted effective null test equivalent to computable martingale betting
records.measure_assumptions: for each n, local bounds imply μ(V_n)≤2^-n; Definition 5 of SRC-0024 gives the three exact grading inequalities
records.relativization: not treated in the inspected source record
records.formal_summary: A Martin-Löf test is computably graded when a computable f supplies the local measure bounds and prefix-free additivity/subadditivity conditions of SRC-0024 Definition 5; passing all such tests characterizes computable randomness.
